board_events.caption: The Mumbai local jerk: feet move with the floor, torso stays behind

board_events.text: A body continues in its state of rest, or of uniform motion in a straight line, unless compelled by a net external force to change that state.
Nothing threw you backward. The lurch is the ABSENCE of a force on your torso, not the presence of one.
Constant velocity - including zero velocity - is the FREE state. It needs no force to maintain.
Inertia = the reluctance of matter to change whatever state of motion it is already in.
How much inertia a body has is measured by its MASS. Loaded goods wagon vs empty handcart. Cricket ball vs shot-put.
Newton's laws hold only in INERTIAL frames. Inside the jerking train, the phantom backward push is a fictitious force.

segments.text: <curious> Picture yourself standing in a crowded Mumbai local, no handrail in reach, when the train suddenly jerks forward to leave the platform. You lurch backward. Nobody pushed you. So what threw you?
Nothing did. Your feet moved with the floor, but your upper body, for just a heartbeat, stayed where it was. The train did not push you backward. It ran out from under your lazy upper body.
And that lurch is the whole of Newton's First Law. A body continues in its state of rest, or of uniform motion in a straight line, unless compelled by a net external force to change that state.
Read it again and notice what the law is really about. Not motion. Change. Your body was at rest, and a body at rest genuinely wants to stay at rest.
So constant velocity, and that includes zero velocity, is the free state. It costs nothing to maintain. You need a force only when you want to change it.
The name for that stubbornness is inertia. It is the reluctance of matter to change whatever state of motion it is already in. Not a force, not a push. Just a refusal.

How much inertia a body has is measured by its mass. A loaded goods wagon is brutal to get rolling and brutal to stop; an empty handcart is not. A cricket ball can be redirected with a flick of the bat. Try that flick on a shot put and you will hurt your wrists.

One catch for the exam. Newton's laws hold only in inertial frames, meaning frames that are not themselves accelerating. Inside that jerking train you seem pushed backward, and that force is fictitious, an artefact of a non-inertial frame.
<curious> सोचिए आप एक crowded Mumbai local में खड़े हैं, कोई handrail पकड़ने को नहीं, और train अचानक झटके से चल पड़ती है। आप पीछे lurch कर जाते हैं। किसी ने धक्का नहीं दिया। तो फेंका किसने?
किसी ने नहीं। आपके feet floor के साथ चले गए, पर upper body एक heartbeat के लिए वहीं रह गया। Train ने आपको push नहीं किया। वो आपके आलसी upper body के नीचे से निकल गई।
और यही पूरा Newton's First Law है। एक body अपनी state of rest में, या straight line में uniform motion में, तब तक बनी रहती है जब तक कोई net external force उसे बदलने पर मजबूर न करे।
अब ध्यान से देखिए law असल में किस बारे में है। Motion के बारे में नहीं। Change के बारे में। आपकी body rest पर थी, और rest पर पड़ी body सच में rest पर ही रहना चाहती है।
तो constant velocity, और उसमें zero velocity भी शामिल है, वो free state है। उसे maintain करने में कुछ नहीं लगता। Force तब चाहिए जब आप उसे बदलना चाहें।
इस ज़िद का नाम है inertia। ये matter की वो अनिच्छा है कि वो अपनी चल रही state of motion को बदले। ना कोई force, ना कोई push। बस एक इनकार।

किसी body में कितना inertia है, ये उसके mass से नापा जाता है। भरा goods wagon चलाना और रोकना दोनों मुश्किल; खाली handcart नहीं। Cricket ball को bat के एक flick से मोड़ा जा सकता है। वही flick shot put पर लगाइए और wrist टूट जाएगी।

Exam के लिए एक catch। Newton's laws सिर्फ inertial frames में चलते हैं, यानी वो frames जो खुद accelerate नहीं कर रहे। उस train के अंदर लगता है कोई पीछे धकेल रहा है, पर वो force fictitious है, non-inertial frame का नतीजा।

board_events.text: A truck crawling at 5 km/h and a motorbike racing at 80 km/h can carry comparable momentum - the truck makes up in mass what it lacks in speed.
Newton's Second Law, in its truest form
A force is not a thing a body HAS. It is an interaction that changes a body's momentum.

When the change happens over a short, violent instant - bat on ball, car on crash barrier - we stop caring about the force at each microsecond and care only about the total kick. That total kick is IMPULSE.

segments.text: Now bring motion into the picture and you get momentum. Written p equals m v, it is literally how much motion a body carries, accounting for both how heavy it is and how fast it is going.
Notice it is a vector, inherited straight from velocity. That vector nature is not decoration - it is where most of the marks in this chapter are won and lost.
Momentum is the quantity Newton actually cared about. Not speed on its own, not mass on its own, but the product.
A truck crawling at five kilometres per hour and a motorbike racing at eighty can carry comparable momentum, because the truck makes up in mass exactly what it lacks in speed.
Which brings us to the Second Law, and to the form your textbook usually shows you second even though it is really first.
Force is the rate at which momentum changes. F equals d p by d t. Push twice as hard, and momentum changes twice as fast. That is the law, complete, with nothing assumed.

Think about it this way. A force is not a thing a body has, sitting in its pocket. It is an interaction, and what that interaction does is change momentum. Speak about force any other way and you will end up confused later.

<excited> And now the payoff. When the momentum change happens over a very short, violent instant, a bat meeting a ball, a foot meeting a football, a car meeting a crash barrier, we stop caring about the exact force at each microsecond. We care only about the total kick delivered. That total kick is impulse, and impulse is simply the change in momentum.
अब motion को picture में लाइए और आपको मिलता है momentum। लिखते हैं p बराबर m v, और ये सचमुच बताता है कि body कितना motion carry कर रही है, mass और speed दोनों को गिनते हुए।
ध्यान दीजिए ये एक vector है, सीधे velocity से मिला हुआ। ये vector nature सजावट नहीं — इसी पर इस chapter के ज़्यादातर marks जीते और हारे जाते हैं।
Momentum ही वो quantity है जिसकी Newton को असल में परवाह थी। अकेली speed नहीं, अकेला mass नहीं, बल्कि दोनों का product।
पाँच kilometre per hour पर रेंगता truck और अस्सी पर भागती motorbike, दोनों का momentum comparable हो सकता है, क्योंकि truck जो speed में कम है वो mass में पूरा कर देता है।
और यहीं से आता है Second Law, वो form जो आपकी textbook अक्सर दूसरे नंबर पर दिखाती है, जबकि असल में वो पहला है।
Force वो rate है जिससे momentum बदलता है। F बराबर d p by d t. दुगना ज़ोर से push कीजिए, momentum दुगनी तेज़ी से बदलेगा। यही law है, पूरा, बिना कोई assumption लिए।
इसे ऐसे सोचिए। Force कोई चीज़ नहीं जो body अपनी जेब में रखती हो। ये एक interaction है, और वो interaction करता क्या है, momentum बदलता है। Force को किसी और तरह से समझा तो आगे जाकर उलझेंगे।

<excited> और अब असली फायदा। जब ये momentum change एक बहुत छोटे, violent instant में होता है, bat से ball का मिलना, पैर से football का, car का crash barrier से, तो हम हर microsecond की exact force की परवाह छोड़ देते हैं। हमें सिर्फ total kick चाहिए। उसी total kick का नाम है impulse, और impulse बस change in momentum है।

sections.title: The Third Law, and where the simple form stops working

board_events.text: Newton's Third Law: forces never come alone

board_events.caption: The bat-ball pair: two arrows, two different bodies

board_events.text: Equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, same line of action.
They act on DIFFERENT bodies - which is exactly why they do not cancel. Tattoo this on your brain before exam day.
Where the simple forms stop working
The form $F = m\vec{a}$ assumes CONSTANT mass. For rockets, falling chains, or sand piling onto a belt, return to the parent form $F = d\vec{p}/dt$.
All of this is non-relativistic: it assumes speeds far below the speed of light, where mass stays constant.

segments.text: Newton's Third Law completes the picture, and it says something stronger than students usually notice. Forces never come alone.
When the bat pushes the ball forward, the ball pushes back on the bat with an equal and opposite force. Not later, not as a response, but at the very same instant. Interactions are always two-sided.
We write it as: the force by A on B equals minus the force by B on A. Equal magnitude, opposite direction, same line of action.
Now here is the part that costs marks. Those two forces act on different bodies. The bat feels one arrow; the ball feels the other.

And that is exactly why they never cancel. Cancelling requires both forces to act on the same body. A Third-Law pair, by construction, never does. Neither the force on the bat nor the force on the ball is cancelled by the other, which is why the ball actually flies.
Before we start deriving things, let us be honest about where these laws quietly stop working.

The friendly form, F equals m a, assumes the mass is constant. For a rocket burning fuel, a chain falling onto a table, or sand piling onto a moving belt, mass is changing, and that form fails. You must return to the parent form, F equals d p by d t.

And all of this is non-relativistic. It assumes speeds far below the speed of light, where mass stays constant. For everything you will meet in N E E T and J E E, that is a safe assumption - but know that it is an assumption.
Newton's Third Law picture को पूरा करता है, और ये उससे ज़्यादा कहता है जितना students आम तौर पर notice करते हैं। Forces कभी अकेली नहीं आतीं।
जब bat ball को आगे push करता है, तो ball भी bat पर उतनी ही और opposite force से push करती है। बाद में नहीं, response की तरह नहीं, बल्कि ठीक उसी instant पर। Interactions हमेशा दो-तरफा होते हैं।
इसे लिखते हैं: force by A on B बराबर minus force by B on A। Equal magnitude, opposite direction, same line of action.
अब वो हिस्सा जो marks खाता है। ये दोनों forces अलग-अलग bodies पर लगती हैं। Bat को एक arrow महसूस होता है; ball को दूसरा।

और इसीलिए वो कभी cancel नहीं होतीं। Cancel होने के लिए दोनों forces का एक ही body पर होना ज़रूरी है। Third-Law pair, अपनी बनावट से ही, ऐसा कभी नहीं करती। ना bat वाली force cancel होती है ना ball वाली, और इसीलिए ball सच में उड़ती है।
Derivations से पहले ईमानदारी से देख लीजिए कि ये laws चुपचाप कहाँ काम करना बंद कर देते हैं।

दोस्ताना form, F बराबर m a, mass को constant मान लेता है। Fuel जलाते rocket के लिए, table पर गिरती chain के लिए, या चलती belt पर गिरती sand के लिए mass बदल रहा है, और ये form fail हो जाता है। तब parent form पर लौटना पड़ेगा, F बराबर d p by d t।

और ये सब non-relativistic है। ये मानकर चलता है कि speeds light की speed से बहुत नीचे हैं, जहाँ mass constant रहता है। N E E T और J E E में जो कुछ आपको मिलेगा, उसके लिए ये safe assumption है — पर याद रखिए ये एक assumption है।

sections.title: Derivation: recovering F = ma from the momentum definition

board_events.text: CBSE Derivation 1: F = ma from the definition of force
Why this form first? Because momentum, not acceleration, is the quantity that force genuinely controls.
ASSUME: the mass of the body is constant. True for almost every Board-level body - a block, a ball, a car of fixed load.

board_events.caption: One parent law, one assumption, two children

board_events.text: Set $F = 0$ and you get $a = 0$: velocity stays constant. The First Law lives INSIDE the Second Law.

segments.text: Our first Board derivation is short, but it reorganises how you think about the whole chapter. We are going to recover F equals m a, rather than assume it.
Begin with the fundamental statement of the Second Law: force is the rate of change of momentum, which is the rate of change of the product m v.

Why start from this form and not the familiar one? Because momentum, not acceleration, is the quantity that force genuinely controls. Acceleration only enters once we make an extra assumption - and it is worth seeing that assumption in the open.

Here it is, stated explicitly: the mass of the body is constant. That is true for almost every body you will meet at Board level. A block, a ball, a car of fixed load. Say it out loud, because the whole derivation hangs on it.
With m constant, it slides straight out of the derivative. Force equals m times d v by d t.
And the rate of change of velocity is, by definition, acceleration. So force equals m a. Not a new law. A special case of the parent law, unlocked by one assumption.
Look at the structure on the board. One parent statement at the top, one assumption in the middle, and the familiar form falls out below. Break the assumption and you fall back up to the parent.

There is a bonus hiding here. Set F equal to zero and you get a equals zero, which means velocity stays constant. That is exactly the First Law's claim. So the First Law lives inside the Second Law, as a special case of a special case.
हमारा पहला Board derivation छोटा है, पर ये पूरे chapter को सोचने का तरीका बदल देता है। हम F बराबर m a को मानेंगे नहीं, उसे recover करेंगे।
शुरू कीजिए Second Law के fundamental statement से: force momentum के change की rate है, यानी product m v के change की rate।

इस form से क्यों शुरू करें, जानी-पहचानी वाली से क्यों नहीं? क्योंकि momentum, ना कि acceleration, वो quantity है जिसे force सचमुच control करता है। Acceleration तभी आता है जब हम एक extra assumption लें — और उस assumption को खुले में देख लेना ज़रूरी है।

ये रहा, साफ़ शब्दों में: body का mass constant है। Board level पर जो भी body आपको मिलेगी, उसके लिए ये सच है। एक block, एक ball, fixed load वाली car। इसे बोलकर कहिए, क्योंकि पूरा derivation इसी पर टंगा है।
m constant होने से वो सीधे derivative के बाहर निकल आता है। Force बराबर m गुणा d v by d t।
और velocity के change की rate, definition से, acceleration है। तो force बराबर m a। कोई नया law नहीं। Parent law का एक special case, जिसे एक assumption ने खोला है।
Board पर structure देखिए। ऊपर एक parent statement, बीच में एक assumption, और नीचे जाना-पहचाना form गिर पड़ता है। Assumption टूटे, तो आप वापस parent पर चढ़ जाते हैं।

यहाँ एक bonus छिपा है। F को zero रखिए तो a zero मिलता है, यानी velocity constant रहती है। यही तो First Law कहता है। मतलब First Law, Second Law के अंदर ही रहता है, special case के अंदर एक special case बनकर।

sections.title: Derivation: the impulse-momentum theorem

board_events.text: CBSE Derivation 2: the Impulse-Momentum Theorem
Take the fundamental form again and multiply both sides by $dt$:
Now integrate over the duration of the interaction, from the instant contact begins to the instant it ends.

board_events.caption: For a variable force, impulse is the area under the force-time graph

board_events.text: We never needed the force at each microsecond. Only the ENDPOINTS of momentum. That is the entire power of the theorem.

segments.text: The second derivation is the workhorse of this subtopic, and it is only three lines long. Take the fundamental form of the Second Law once more.
Force equals d p by d t. Multiply both sides by d t, and you get F d t equals d p. Nothing clever yet - we have only rearranged.
Now integrate. On the left, over time, from the instant contact begins to the instant it ends. On the right, over momentum, from its initial to its final value.
Look at the two sides carefully. The left side is, by definition, the impulse J. The right side is an integral of d p, which collapses immediately to a difference.

So impulse equals final momentum minus initial momentum. Equals m v final minus m v initial. That is the impulse-momentum theorem, and it is exact - no assumption about the force being constant, or smooth, or even knowable.

For a variable force, look at what the left side means graphically. It is the area under the force-time graph. This is the picture N E E T loves to test: two very different curves with the same area deliver the same total kick.

That graph is worth sitting with. A collision force is a spiky, violent, unmeasurable thing. Nobody knows its value at each microsecond. But the area is knowable, because the area equals a change in momentum, and momentum you can measure at the endpoints.
<whisper> And that is the whole power of the theorem. We sidestep the messy force completely. We never needed it. We only needed where the momentum started and where it ended.
दूसरा derivation इस subtopic का workhorse है, और सिर्फ तीन lines का है। Second Law का fundamental form एक बार फिर उठाइए।
Force बराबर d p by d t। दोनों sides को d t से multiply कीजिए, मिलता है F d t बराबर d p। अभी तक कुछ चालाकी नहीं — बस rearrange किया है।
अब integrate कीजिए। बाईं तरफ time पर, उस instant से जब contact शुरू होता है उस instant तक जब खत्म होता है। दाईं तरफ momentum पर, initial से final तक।
दोनों sides को ध्यान से देखिए। बाईं side, definition से, impulse J है। दाईं side d p का integral है, जो तुरंत एक difference में सिमट जाता है।

तो impulse बराबर final momentum minus initial momentum। यानी m v final minus m v initial। यही impulse-momentum theorem है, और ये exact है — force के constant, smooth, या जानने लायक होने की कोई assumption नहीं।

Variable force के लिए देखिए बाईं side का graphically मतलब क्या है। वो force-time graph के नीचे का area है। यही वो picture है जिसे N E E T टेस्ट करना पसंद करता है: बिल्कुल अलग दिखती दो curves, same area, same total kick।

उस graph के साथ थोड़ा बैठिए। Collision की force एक spiky, violent, नापने-लायक-नहीं चीज़ है। हर microsecond पर उसकी value किसी को नहीं पता। पर area पता है, क्योंकि area बराबर change in momentum है, और momentum को आप endpoints पर नाप सकते हैं।
<whisper> और यही theorem की पूरी ताकत है। हम उस गंदी force को पूरी तरह bypass कर देते हैं। हमें उसकी ज़रूरत ही नहीं थी। हमें सिर्फ ये चाहिए था कि momentum कहाँ से शुरू हुआ और कहाँ खत्म।

sections.title: Derivation: conservation of momentum from the Third Law

board_events.text: CBSE Derivation 3: Conservation of Momentum
Consider two bodies A and B interacting with each other and nothing else - an ISOLATED system.

board_events.svg:

<text x="350" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#1a1a1a">Third Law + Second Law = momentum conservation</text>

<text x="80" y="80" font-size="13" fill="#1a1a1a">isolated system: nothing else acts</text>

<text x="350" y="110" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#1f4e79">F(A on B) = dp(B)/dt</text>

</svg>
board_events.caption: Two bodies, one Third-Law pair, and a sum that refuses to change

board_events.text: Add them. The left side vanishes, because by the Third Law the forces are equal and opposite.
The individual momenta change wildly during the interaction. Their SUM does not move at all.
This is the law you will reach for in every recoil, explosion, and collision problem.

segments.text: The third derivation fuses the two laws we have just met, and out drops the most powerful tool in mechanics.
Consider two bodies, A and B, interacting with each other and with nothing else. We call that an isolated system, and the phrase is doing real work: nothing from outside is allowed to touch them.
During their interaction, A exerts a force on B, and by the Third Law, B exerts an equal and opposite force back on A. Two arrows, two bodies, as we drew earlier.
Now apply the Second Law to each body separately. The force on B equals the rate of change of B's momentum. The force on A equals the rate of change of A's momentum.
Add the two equations. And watch the left side. It is the sum of a Third-Law pair, so it is exactly zero. Not approximately, not usually. Exactly.
So the rate of change of the total momentum is zero, which means the total momentum of A plus B is a constant. When no external force acts, the total momentum of the system is conserved.
Sit with how strange that is. During the interaction the individual momenta are changing wildly - A is being slammed, B is being flung. But their sum does not budge by a whisker.

This is the law you will reach for in every recoil, every explosion, and every collision problem for the rest of this chapter. We derived it from the Third Law, but from here on we will simply use it.
तीसरा derivation उन दोनों laws को जोड़ता है जो हमने अभी देखे, और बाहर निकलता है mechanics का सबसे ताकतवर tool।
दो bodies लीजिए, A और B, जो सिर्फ एक-दूसरे से interact कर रही हैं और किसी और से नहीं। इसे कहते हैं isolated system, और ये phrase असली काम कर रहा है: बाहर से किसी को छूने की इजाज़त नहीं।
Interaction के दौरान A, B पर एक force लगाता है, और Third Law से B भी A पर उतनी ही और opposite force लगाता है। दो arrows, दो bodies, जैसा हमने पहले draw किया था।
अब हर body पर अलग से Second Law लगाइए। B पर force बराबर B के momentum के change की rate। A पर force बराबर A के momentum के change की rate।
दोनों equations को जोड़िए। और बाईं side देखिए। वो एक Third-Law pair का sum है, तो वो ठीक zero है। लगभग नहीं, आम तौर पर नहीं। बिल्कुल zero।
तो total momentum के change की rate zero है, यानी A plus B का total momentum एक constant है। जब कोई external force नहीं लगता, system का total momentum conserve रहता है।
थोड़ा सोचिए ये कितनी अजीब बात है। Interaction के दौरान individual momenta बुरी तरह बदल रहे हैं — A को झटका लग रहा है, B उछल रहा है। पर उनका sum रत्ती भर नहीं हिलता।
यही वो law है जिसे आप इस chapter के हर recoil, हर explosion, और हर collision problem में उठाएँगे। हमने इसे Third Law से derive किया, पर अब आगे से हम इसे बस इस्तेमाल करेंगे।

sections.title: Newton's Laws and Impulse: the formula set

board_events.text: Subtopic 1 - key formulas and definitions
Linear momentum: $m$ in kg, $v$ in m/s. SI unit kg m s$^{-1}$, equivalently N s. Dimensions $[M^1 L^1 T^{-1}]$.
Force: SI unit newton, N = kg m s$^{-2}$. Dimensions $[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}]$.
Impulse and momentum share the dimensional formula $[M L T^{-1}]$, so N s and kg m/s are the SAME unit. NEET loves this.

segments.text: Let us gather the toolkit for this subtopic in one place, so you can jump here for a fast revision without re-watching the derivations.
First, linear momentum. p equals m v, a vector pointing along the velocity.
Mass in kilograms, velocity in metres per second, so the S I unit is kilogram metre per second, which is the same as a newton second. Dimensions: M to the one, L to the one, T to the minus one.
Next, the Second Law, in both its forms. Force is the rate of change of momentum, always. And for constant mass only, force equals m a.
Force is measured in newtons, and a newton is a kilogram metre per second squared. Dimensions: M to the one, L to the one, T to the minus two.
Impulse for a constant force is simply force times the time interval.
For a variable force it is the integral of F d t, which is the area under the force-time graph. That second reading is the one that rescues you when the force is spiky.

The impulse-momentum theorem ties them together: impulse equals the change in momentum. And rearranging gives the average force during an impact, delta p over delta t. These two are your Board numericals.
And conservation: if the net external force is zero, initial momentum equals final momentum, and the sum of m v over all bodies stays constant.

<whisper> Now the detail that wins a free mark. Impulse and momentum share the dimensional formula M L T to the minus one. So a newton second and a kilogram metre per second are the same unit wearing different clothes. Examiners test this directly.
इस subtopic की पूरी toolkit एक जगह इकट्ठा कर लेते हैं, ताकि fast revision के लिए आप सीधे यहाँ आ सकें, derivations दोबारा देखे बिना।
सबसे पहले linear momentum। p बराबर m v, एक vector जो velocity की दिशा में point करता है।
Mass kilogram में, velocity metre per second में, तो S I unit हुआ kilogram metre per second, जो newton second के बराबर ही है। Dimensions: M की power one, L की power one, T की power minus one।
अगला, Second Law, दोनों forms में। Force हमेशा momentum के change की rate है। और सिर्फ constant mass के लिए, force बराबर m a।
Force newton में नापी जाती है, और एक newton यानी kilogram metre per second squared। Dimensions: M की power one, L की power one, T की power minus two।
Constant force के लिए impulse बस force गुणा time interval है।
Variable force के लिए ये F d t का integral है, यानी force-time graph के नीचे का area। यही दूसरा पढ़ना आपको तब बचाता है जब force spiky हो।
Impulse-momentum theorem दोनों को जोड़ता है: impulse बराबर change in momentum। और rearrange करने पर impact के दौरान average force मिलता है, delta p upon delta t। यही दोनों आपके Board numericals हैं।
और conservation: अगर net external force zero है, तो initial momentum बराबर final momentum, और सारी bodies पर m v का sum constant रहता है।

<whisper> अब वो detail जो मुफ़्त का mark दिलाती है। Impulse और momentum का dimensional formula एक ही है, M L T की power minus one। तो newton second और kilogram metre per second एक ही unit हैं, बस कपड़े अलग हैं। Examiners इसे सीधे पूछते हैं।

sections.title: Worked Example 1 [CBSE Board]: the cricket ball

board_events.text: Example 1 [CBSE Board Level]

A cricket ball of mass 0.16 kg moves toward a batsman at 30 m/s. He hits it straight back along the same line at 40 m/s. Contact time 0.01 s. Find (a) the impulse imparted, (b) the average force by the bat.

board_events.svg:

board_events.text: Step 1 - Fix a sign convention. Take the direction away from the batsman (the final direction) as positive.
A student who writes $J = 0.16(40 - 30) = 1.6$ N s forgot the ball reversed direction, and loses almost everything.

segments.text: Our first worked example is a Board-level classic, and the marks in it are won in a place most students skip entirely.

A cricket ball of mass zero point one six kilograms moves toward a batsman at thirty metres per second. He hits it straight back at forty. Contact lasts one hundredth of a second. Find the impulse imparted to the ball, and the average force the bat exerts.
Before touching a formula, look at the figure. The ball came in one way and left the other way. That reversal is the whole problem.
So step one, and this is where the marks live: fix a sign convention. Take the direction away from the batsman, which is the final direction, as positive. Write that down on your answer sheet.
Then the incoming velocity is minus thirty metres per second, and the outgoing velocity is plus forty. The minus sign is not decoration. It is physics.

Now apply the impulse-momentum theorem. J equals m v final minus m v initial. That is zero point one six times plus forty, minus zero point one six times minus thirty. Subtracting a negative adds, so we get six point four plus four point eight - eleven point two newton seconds, away from the batsman.

And the average force is just impulse over contact time. Eleven point two divided by one hundredth of a second gives one thousand one hundred and twenty newtons - roughly the weight of a small car, delivered in a blink.

<whisper> Now the trap. A student who writes J equals zero point one six times forty minus thirty, and reports one point six newton seconds, has forgotten the ball reversed. Same numbers, wrong physics, almost no marks. Fix the direction before you substitute.
हमारा पहला worked example एक Board-level classic है, और इसके marks वहाँ जीते जाते हैं जहाँ ज़्यादातर students कूद जाते हैं।

Zero point one six kilogram की एक cricket ball batsman की तरफ तीस metre per second से आ रही है। वो उसे सीधा वापस चालीस पर मारता है। Contact एक सौवें second का है। Ball को दिया impulse निकालिए, और bat की average force।
Formula छूने से पहले figure देखिए। Ball एक तरफ से आई और दूसरी तरफ चली गई। यही reversal पूरी problem है।
तो step one, और यहीं marks रहते हैं: sign convention fix कीजिए। Batsman से दूर की direction, यानी final direction, को positive लीजिए। इसे answer sheet पर लिख दीजिए।
तब incoming velocity हुई minus तीस metre per second, और outgoing velocity plus चालीस। वो minus sign सजावट नहीं है। वो physics है।

अब impulse-momentum theorem लगाइए। J बराबर m v final minus m v initial। यानी zero point one six गुणा plus चालीस, minus zero point one six गुणा minus तीस। Negative को घटाना जोड़ना बन जाता है, तो मिला छह point चार plus चार point आठ, यानी ग्यारह point दो newton second, batsman से दूर की तरफ।
और average force बस impulse upon contact time है। ग्यारह point दो को एक सौवें second से भाग दीजिए, मिलता है एक हज़ार एक सौ बीस newtons। ये लगभग एक छोटी car का weight है, पलक झपकते दे दिया गया।

<whisper> अब trap। जो student लिखता है J बराबर zero point one six गुणा चालीस minus तीस, और एक point छह newton second बताता है, वो भूल गया कि ball पलटी थी। वही numbers, गलत physics, लगभग zero marks। Substitute करने से पहले direction fix कीजिए।

sections.title: Worked Example 2 [NEET Speed Trap]: rifle recoil

board_events.text: Example 2 [NEET Speed Trap]
A rifle of mass 4 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g with a muzzle speed of 400 m/s. What is the recoil speed of the rifle?
The trap: students start writing energy equations, or hunting for the force. Don't.
The word 'fires', with no external horizontal force, SCREAMS conservation of momentum.

segments.text: This one is a N E E T speed trap, which means the physics is easy and the clock is the real opponent.
A rifle of mass four kilograms fires a bullet of mass twenty grams with a muzzle speed of four hundred metres per second. What is the recoil speed of the rifle?

Here is the trap. Students see a fired bullet and start writing energy equations, or go hunting for the force between the powder gases and the barrel. Both are dead ends that will cost you a minute you do not have.

The tell is the word 'fires'. An explosion inside the rifle, no external horizontal force worth speaking of. That combination screams conservation of momentum, and it should be a reflex, not a deduction.
So look at the figure. Before firing, everything is at rest, so the total momentum is zero. After firing, the total must still be zero. The two momenta have no choice but to cancel.
Which means mass of bullet times speed of bullet equals mass of rifle times speed of rifle, in magnitude.

Convert twenty grams to zero point zero two kilograms instantly. Then zero point zero two times four hundred is eight - a deliberately clean number. Divide by four and the recoil speed is two metres per second, opposite to the bullet.

And a free elimination. If an option offers two metres per second in the same direction as the bullet, strike it out on physics alone, without arithmetic. Recoil is always backward. Spot conservation on sight and this is a ten-second problem.
ये एक N E E T speed trap है, मतलब physics आसान है और असली दुश्मन घड़ी है।
चार kilogram का एक rifle बीस gram की bullet को चार सौ metre per second की muzzle speed से fire करता है। Rifle की recoil speed क्या है?

अब trap। Students fired bullet देखते ही energy equations लिखने लगते हैं, या powder gases और barrel के बीच की force ढूँढने निकल पड़ते हैं। दोनों dead end हैं और वो एक minute खा जाएँगे जो आपके पास है ही नहीं।
इशारा है 'fires' शब्द। Rifle के अंदर एक explosion, बाहर कोई काम की horizontal force नहीं। ये combination चीख़कर कहता है conservation of momentum, और ये reflex होना चाहिए, deduction नहीं।
तो figure देखिए। Firing से पहले सब कुछ rest पर है, तो total momentum zero है। Firing के बाद भी total zero ही रहेगा। दोनों momenta के पास cancel होने के अलावा कोई चारा नहीं।
यानी mass of bullet गुणा speed of bullet बराबर mass of rifle गुणा speed of rifle, magnitude में।

बीस gram को तुरंत zero point zero two kilogram कीजिए। फिर zero point zero two गुणा चार सौ हुआ आठ — जानबूझकर साफ़ number। चार से भाग दीजिए और recoil speed आती है दो metre per second, bullet के उल्टी दिशा में।

और एक मुफ़्त elimination। अगर कोई option दो metre per second bullet की same direction में बताए, तो उसे बिना arithmetic के, सिर्फ physics से काट दीजिए। Recoil हमेशा पीछे की तरफ होता है। Conservation दिखते ही पहचान लीजिए और ये दस second की problem है।

sections.title: Worked Example 3 [JEE Main]: impulse from a floor

board_events.text: Example 3 [JEE Main Level]
A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 5 m onto a hard floor and rebounds to a height of 1.8 m. Find the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the ball by the floor. Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$.

board_events.text: Step 3 - Take upward as positive, so $v_1 = -10$ m/s and $v_2 = +6$ m/s.
The impulse already accounts for the energy lost in the bounce - we never assumed the speeds were equal, because they were not.

segments.text: This J E E Main example is a two-chapter question in disguise. It links kinematics to the impulse-momentum theorem, and you have to notice the join.

A ball of mass zero point five kilograms is dropped from five metres onto a hard floor and rebounds to one point eight metres. Find the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the ball by the floor. Take g as ten metres per second squared.
Look at the figure first. You are given heights, but the theorem speaks in speeds. So the first job is translation: heights in, speeds out.

Speed just before impact comes from free fall through five metres. v one equals root two g h, which is root of two times ten times five, equals root of one hundred, equals ten metres per second, downward.

Speed just after impact comes from the rebound height. It rises to one point eight metres, so v two equals root of two times ten times one point eight, equals root thirty six, equals six metres per second, upward.
Now step three, and it is the same discipline as the cricket ball. Take upward as positive. Then v one is minus ten and v two is plus six.
Apply the theorem. J equals zero point five times plus six, minus zero point five times minus ten. That is three plus five, equals eight newton seconds, directed upward.

<curious> Now notice what we quietly did not do. We never assumed the two speeds were equal, because they were not - ten in, six out. The bounce lost energy, and our impulse already accounts for it. We also ignored gravity's impulse during the brief contact, because it is negligible next to the floor's.
ये J E E Main example असल में भेस बदले हुए दो chapters का सवाल है। ये kinematics को impulse-momentum theorem से जोड़ता है, और वो जोड़ आपको पकड़ना है।

Zero point five kilogram की एक ball पाँच metre से hard floor पर गिराई जाती है और एक point आठ metre तक rebound करती है। Floor द्वारा दिए impulse की magnitude निकालिए। g को दस metre per second squared लीजिए।
पहले figure देखिए। आपको heights दी गई हैं, पर theorem speeds की भाषा बोलता है। तो पहला काम है translation: heights अंदर, speeds बाहर।
Impact से ठीक पहले की speed पाँच metre की free fall से आती है। v one बराबर root two g h, यानी root of two गुणा दस गुणा पाँच, बराबर root सौ, यानी दस metre per second, नीचे।
Impact के ठीक बाद की speed rebound height से आती है। वो एक point आठ metre तक चढ़ती है, तो v two बराबर root of two गुणा दस गुणा एक point आठ, बराबर root छत्तीस, यानी छह metre per second, ऊपर की तरफ।
अब step three, और ये वही discipline है जो cricket ball में थी। ऊपर की तरफ को positive लीजिए। तब v one है minus दस और v two है plus छह।
Theorem लगाइए। J बराबर zero point five गुणा plus छह, minus zero point five गुणा minus दस। यानी तीन plus पाँच, बराबर आठ newton second, ऊपर की तरफ।

<curious> अब देखिए हमने चुपचाप क्या नहीं किया। हमने कभी नहीं माना कि दोनों speeds बराबर हैं — दस अंदर, छह बाहर। Bounce में energy गई, और हमारा impulse उस loss को गिन चुका है। Contact के छोटे वक़्त में gravity का impulse छोड़ दिया, क्योंकि floor के मुक़ाबले वो negligible है।

sections.title: Worked Example 4 [JEE Advanced]: sand on a conveyor belt

board_events.text: Example 4 [JEE Advanced Level]

Dry sand falls vertically at 3 kg/s from a stationary hopper onto a horizontal conveyor belt moving at a constant 2 m/s. Find (a) the motor's horizontal force, (b) the rate of KE gain by the sand, (c) the rate of work by the motor. Explain any discrepancy.
Variable-mass problem: $F = m\vec{a}$ FAILS here. You must use $F = d\vec{p}/dt$.

<text x="505" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#1e8449">sand gains KE at only 6 W</text>
<text x="505" y="296" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b">missing 6 W = friction heat while grains slip</text>
</svg>
board_events.caption: Each second, 3 kg of sand must be accelerated from rest to belt speed

board_events.text: 12 W in, only 6 W into the sand. The missing 6 W is dissipated as friction heat while each grain is dragged up to belt speed. Exactly half the work lost to friction is the signature of this problem class.

segments.text: Now a J E E Advanced problem that exists purely to punish anyone who reaches for F equals m a by reflex.

Dry sand falls at three kilograms per second from a stationary hopper onto a horizontal conveyor belt moving at a constant two metres per second. Find the horizontal force the motor must supply, the rate at which kinetic energy is delivered to the sand, and the rate at which the motor does work. Then explain the discrepancy.
First, classify it. The mass being carried by the belt is growing every second. This is a variable-mass problem, and here the constant-mass form fails outright. You must use force equals d p by d t.

Look at the figure and read the physics off it. Each second, three kilograms of sand lands. The instant it lands, it has zero horizontal velocity. The belt must accelerate it up to two metres per second.

So the horizontal momentum gained per second is u times d m by d t, which is two times three, equals six newtons. There is no m d v by d t term at all, because the belt runs at constant speed - every bit of the force accelerates new sand.
Part b. The sand ends up moving at two metres per second, so the kinetic energy delivered per second is half times d m by d t times u squared. Half times three times four, equals six watts.
Part c. The motor's six newton force acts on a belt surface moving at two metres per second, so its power is force times speed, equals twelve watts. And there is the discrepancy staring at you.

<curious> Twelve watts in, but the sand gains only six. Where did half the work go? Into friction heat, during the brief slipping while each grain is dragged up to belt speed. That factor of two is not a coincidence - it is the signature of this problem class.
अब एक J E E Advanced problem जो सिर्फ इसलिए बनी है कि reflex में F बराबर m a उठाने वालों को सज़ा दे।

Sookhi sand एक hopper से तीन kilogram per second की दर से गिर रही है, एक conveyor belt पर जो constant दो metre per second से चल रही है। Motor को कितनी horizontal force देनी होगी, sand को kinetic energy किस rate से मिल रही है, और motor किस rate से work कर रहा है। फिर discrepancy समझाइए।
पहले इसे classify कीजिए। Belt जो mass carry कर रही है वो हर second बढ़ रहा है। ये variable-mass problem है, और यहाँ constant-mass form सीधे fail है। आपको force बराबर d p by d t इस्तेमाल करना ही होगा।
Figure देखिए और physics उसी से पढ़िए। हर second तीन kilogram sand गिरती है। गिरते ही उसकी horizontal velocity zero है। Belt को उसे दो metre per second तक accelerate करना है।

तो हर second gain हुआ horizontal momentum है u गुणा d m by d t, यानी दो गुणा तीन, बराबर छह newton। यहाँ m d v by d t term है ही नहीं, क्योंकि belt constant speed पर है — पूरी force नई sand को accelerate करती है।
Part b। Sand आखिर में दो metre per second से चलती है, तो हर second दी गई kinetic energy है half गुणा d m by d t गुणा u squared। Half गुणा तीन गुणा चार, बराबर छह watt।
Part c। Motor की छह newton की force उस belt surface पर लगती है जो दो metre per second से चल रही है, तो power बराबर force गुणा speed, यानी बारह watt। और discrepancy आपके सामने खड़ी है।

<curious> बारह watt अंदर, पर sand को मिले सिर्फ छह। आधा work गया कहाँ? Friction की heat में, उस slipping के दौरान जब हर दाना belt speed तक घसीटा जाता है। ये factor of two इत्तेफ़ाक़ नहीं — यही इस problem class की पहचान है।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: Newton's Laws and Impulse

board_events.text: Common student pitfalls
Forgetting that momentum and impulse are VECTORS. The single biggest source of lost marks in this chapter.

When a ball reverses direction its speed may be unchanged, but its velocity changes sign - so $\Delta p$ can be as large as $2mv$, not zero. Always fix a positive direction before substituting numbers.
Believing action-reaction forces cancel. They are equal and opposite, but they act on TWO DIFFERENT bodies, so they never cancel on a single body.
Using $F = m\vec{a}$ when mass changes. Rockets, falling chains, sand-on-belts, leaking trolleys: the moment mass is variable, retreat to $F = d\vec{p}/dt$.
Confusing inertia with weight. Inertia depends only on mass and is the same on the Moon as on Earth. Weight is the gravitational force and changes with $g$.
Pro-tip: the units sanity check
Impulse and momentum share the dimensional formula $[MLT^{-1}]$, so N s and kg m/s are the same unit.

If you ever derive an 'impulse' that comes out in joules or newtons, you have made an algebra error. Stop and recheck before committing. This five-second check catches more mistakes than any other in this chapter.

segments.text: Every subtopic ends with the traps, because knowing the physics and losing the marks anyway is the real exam failure mode. Here are the four worst.
Number one, and it is the biggest source of lost marks in this whole chapter: forgetting that momentum and impulse are vectors.

When a ball reverses, its speed may be unchanged but its velocity changes sign. So the change in momentum can be as large as two m v, not zero. Fix a positive direction before you substitute a single number. Both our impulse examples turned on this.

Number two: believing action-reaction forces cancel. They are equal and opposite, yes. But they act on two different bodies, so they never cancel on any single body. If they did, nothing could ever accelerate.

Number three: using F equals m a when the mass changes. Rockets, falling chains, sand on belts, leaking trolleys. The moment mass is variable, retreat to F equals d p by d t - as the conveyor belt showed.

Number four: confusing inertia with weight. Inertia depends only on mass and is the same on the Moon as on Earth; weight is the gravitational force and changes with g. A heavy crate is hard to push in deep space too - that is inertia.
And now the pro-tip that pays for itself every single time.
Impulse and momentum share the dimensional formula M L T to the minus one, which means a newton second and a kilogram metre per second are the same unit.

<whisper> So if you ever derive an impulse that comes out in joules, or in newtons, you have made an algebra error. Stop and recheck before committing the answer. This five-second check catches more mistakes than any other habit in this chapter.
हर subtopic traps पर खत्म होता है, क्योंकि physics आती हो और फिर भी marks जाएँ — यही असली exam failure है। ये रहे सबसे बुरे चार।
नंबर एक, और पूरे chapter में सबसे ज़्यादा marks यही खाता है: ये भूल जाना कि momentum और impulse vectors हैं।
जब ball पलटती है, speed भले ना बदले, पर velocity का sign बदल जाता है। तो change in momentum दो m v जितना बड़ा हो सकता है, zero नहीं। Number substitute करने से पहले positive direction fix कीजिए।

नंबर दो: ये मानना कि action-reaction forces cancel हो जाती हैं। वो equal और opposite हैं, पर दो अलग bodies पर लगती हैं, तो किसी एक body पर कभी cancel नहीं होतीं। हो जातीं, तो कुछ कभी accelerate ना कर पाता।
नंबर तीन: mass बदलने पर F बराबर m a इस्तेमाल करना। Rockets, गिरती chains, belt पर sand, टपकती trolleys। जैसे ही mass variable हो, F बराबर d p by d t पर लौट आइए — जैसा conveyor belt ने दिखाया।

नंबर चार: inertia को weight समझ लेना। Inertia सिर्फ mass पर depend करता है और Moon पर वही है जो Earth पर; weight gravitational force है और g के साथ बदलता है। भारी crate deep space में भी मुश्किल है — वो inertia है।
और अब वो pro-tip जो हर बार अपनी कीमत वसूल कर लेता है।
Impulse और momentum का dimensional formula एक ही है, M L T की power minus one, यानी newton second और kilogram metre per second एक ही unit हैं।

<whisper> तो अगर कभी आपका निकाला impulse joules में आ जाए, या newtons में, तो algebra में गलती हुई है। Answer commit करने से पहले रुकिए और दोबारा check कीजिए। ये पाँच second का check इस chapter की किसी भी और आदत से ज़्यादा गलतियाँ पकड़ता है।

sections.title: The books must balance: conservation of linear momentum

board_events.text: Where does the Diwali rocket's motion come from?

board_events.caption: Total momentum was zero before lighting, and it is still zero after

board_events.text: The total 'amount of motion' of rocket-plus-gas was zero before lighting, and it stays zero after. It gets REDISTRIBUTED, not created.
The gas rushes down carrying a big chunk of downward momentum, so the rocket must carry an equal chunk upward to keep the books balanced.
The principle of conservation of linear momentum
We already proved WHY in Subtopic 1: internal forces always come in equal-and-opposite Third-Law pairs that cancel. Here we focus on USING it.
Stand on a skateboard and throw a heavy bag forward: you roll backward. Step off a small boat onto a jetty: the boat scoots away. Fire a rifle: it kicks into your shoulder.

segments.text: You have seen this on every Diwali. A rocket sits still on the ground, then a jet of hot gas blasts downward and the rocket streaks up. Nobody is pushing the rocket from above. So where does its upward motion come from?
Look at the two panels. Before lighting, nothing is moving, so the total momentum of rocket plus gas is exactly zero. After lighting, that total is still exactly zero.
Here is the secret. The total amount of motion did not appear from anywhere. It got redistributed. Nothing was created; it was only shared out.
The gas rushes downward carrying a big chunk of downward momentum. So the rocket must carry an equal chunk of upward momentum, purely to keep the books balanced. The grand total never changes.
This is the principle of conservation of linear momentum, and it is arguably the single most powerful problem-solving tool you will meet in all of mechanics.
If the net external force on a system is zero, then the sum of m u over all bodies before equals the sum of m v over all bodies after. That is it. That is the whole statement.

And we already proved why it is true, back in the last subtopic. Internal forces always come in equal-and-opposite Third-Law pairs that cancel in the sum. Here we are not going to re-prove it. We are going to use it.

The everyday versions are everywhere. Stand on a skateboard and throw a heavy bag forward, and you roll backward. Step off a small wooden boat onto a jetty, and the boat scoots away behind you. Fire a rifle and it kicks into your shoulder. In every case, you push something one way and the system pushes you the other, so the total is unchanged.

ये आपने हर Diwali पर देखा है। एक rocket ज़मीन पर चुपचाप खड़ा है, फिर गरम gas का jet नीचे की तरफ निकलता है और rocket ऊपर छूट जाता है। ऊपर से तो कोई rocket को push नहीं कर रहा। तो उसकी ऊपर वाली motion आई कहाँ से?
दोनों panels देखिए। Lighting से पहले कुछ नहीं चल रहा, तो rocket plus gas का total momentum ठीक zero है। Lighting के बाद भी वो total ठीक zero ही है।
यहाँ राज़ ये है। कुल motion कहीं से पैदा नहीं हुई। वो बस redistribute हो गई। कुछ बना नहीं; सिर्फ बँटा है।
Gas नीचे की तरफ भागती है और downward momentum का बड़ा हिस्सा ले जाती है। तो rocket को upward momentum का उतना ही हिस्सा उठाना पड़ेगा, सिर्फ इसलिए कि हिसाब बराबर रहे। Grand total कभी नहीं बदलता।
यही है principle of conservation of linear momentum, और दलील दी जा सकती है कि पूरी mechanics में ये आपका सबसे ताकतवर problem-solving tool है।
अगर किसी system पर net external force zero है, तो पहले सारी bodies पर m u का sum बराबर होगा बाद में m v के sum के। बस। यही पूरा statement है।

और हम पिछले subtopic में ये prove कर चुके हैं कि ये सच क्यों है। Internal forces हमेशा equal-and-opposite Third-Law pairs में आती हैं जो sum में cancel हो जाती हैं। यहाँ हम इसे दोबारा prove नहीं करेंगे। यहाँ हम इसे इस्तेमाल करेंगे।

रोज़मर्रा के version हर जगह हैं। Skateboard पर खड़े होकर भारी bag आगे फेंकिए, आप पीछे लुढ़क जाएँगे। छोटी लकड़ी की boat से jetty पर उतरिए, boat पीछे खिसक जाएगी। Rifle चलाइए, वो कंधे में लात मारेगी। हर बार आप किसी चीज़ को एक तरफ धकेलते हैं और system आपको दूसरी तरफ, ताकि total वही रहे।

board_events.caption: Three problem families, and the separate question of kinetic energy

board_events.text: RECOIL AND EXPLOSIONS - one body becomes two (or more) that fly apart.
COLLISIONS - two bodies meet, interact briefly, and separate (or stick together).
VARIABLE-MASS SYSTEMS - rockets, falling chains, raindrops growing as they fall.
A vital companion idea: elastic versus inelastic
Momentum is conserved in EVERY collision, as long as external forces are negligible during the brief impact. Kinetic energy is a different matter entirely.
KE is conserved only in a perfectly ELASTIC collision - two carrom coins, near-ideal billiard balls.
In a real-world crunch - cars crumpling, clay hitting a wall - some KE converts to heat, sound and deformation: INELASTIC. If the bodies stick together, PERFECTLY inelastic.

segments.text: This single idea cracks open three big families of problems, and it is worth naming them now, because every question you meet will belong to one of them.
Family one: recoil and explosions. One body becomes two, or more, that fly apart. The rifle, the Diwali rocket, a shell bursting in mid-air.
Family two: collisions. Two bodies meet, interact briefly, and then separate - or stick together and travel as one. Carrom coins, railway wagons coupling, a bullet burying itself in a block.
Family three: variable-mass systems. Rockets burning fuel, chains falling onto tables, raindrops growing as they fall. This family is where J E E Advanced lives.
Now a companion idea that decides which tool you are allowed to use, and getting it wrong destroys otherwise perfect solutions.
Momentum is conserved in every collision, as long as external forces are negligible during the brief impact. Every single one. There is no exception you will meet at this level.

Kinetic energy is a completely different matter. It is conserved only in a perfectly elastic collision - think two carrom coins, or near-ideal billiard balls, where the bodies bounce apart with nothing lost.
In a real-world crunch, two cars crumpling, a ball of clay hitting a wall, some kinetic energy converts into heat, sound and permanent deformation. That collision is inelastic.

And if the bodies stick together and move off as one lump, it is perfectly inelastic - the extreme case, where the maximum possible kinetic energy is lost. Keep these labels sharp; the next few examples turn on them.
यही एक idea तीन बड़े problem families खोल देता है, और इन्हें अभी नाम दे देना ठीक रहेगा, क्योंकि आपको मिलने वाला हर सवाल इन्हीं में से किसी एक का होगा।
Family एक: recoil और explosions। एक body दो, या उससे ज़्यादा, में बँटकर उड़ जाती है। Rifle, Diwali का rocket, हवा में फटता shell।
Family दो: collisions। दो bodies मिलती हैं, थोड़ी देर interact करती हैं, फिर अलग हो जाती हैं — या चिपककर एक बनकर चलती हैं। Carrom के coins, जुड़ते railway wagons, block में धँसती bullet।
Family तीन: variable-mass systems। Fuel जलाते rockets, table पर गिरती chains, गिरते-गिरते बड़ी होती raindrops। इसी family में J E E Advanced रहता है।
अब एक companion idea जो तय करता है कि आपको कौन सा tool इस्तेमाल करने की इजाज़त है, और इसे गलत समझना वरना perfect solutions को तबाह कर देता है।
Momentum हर collision में conserve होता है, बशर्ते उस छोटे से impact के दौरान external forces negligible हों। हर एक में। इस level पर आपको कोई exception नहीं मिलेगा।

Kinetic energy बिल्कुल अलग मामला है। वो सिर्फ perfectly elastic collision में conserve होती है — सोचिए carrom के दो coins, या near-ideal billiard balls, जहाँ bodies बिना कुछ खोए उछलकर अलग हो जाती हैं।
असली दुनिया की टक्कर में, दो cars का कुचलना, दीवार पर clay की ball, कुछ kinetic energy heat, sound और permanent deformation में बदल जाती है। वो collision inelastic है।

और अगर bodies चिपककर एक ढेले की तरह चल पड़ें, तो वो perfectly inelastic है — वो extreme case जहाँ ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा kinetic energy खोती है। इन labels को धार पर रखिए; अगले कुछ examples इन्हीं पर घूमेंगे।

sections.title: The 'no doors' condition: when you may NOT conserve momentum

board_events.text: Think about it this way: money in a sealed room
People inside can hand cash to each other all day - those are the internal forces - but not a single rupee can enter or leave. The total is fixed, even as individual wallets fatten and thin.
The 'no doors' condition IS the requirement that no net external force acts. It is the crucial one.

board_events.text: It applies COMPONENT-WISE. If the net external force is zero only along one axis, momentum is conserved along that axis alone.
During a quick collision or explosion, the internal impulsive forces are enormous compared to gravity or friction - so we treat the system as effectively isolated for that instant.
But over longer times, external forces DO change momentum. Apply conservation only ACROSS THE INSTANT of impact.
Choosing the system correctly is everything. Pick the system so the troublesome forces become internal.

segments.text: <curious> Think about it this way. Picture momentum as money in a sealed room with no doors. That room is your isolated system.

People inside can hand cash to each other all day long - those handovers are the internal forces - but not a single rupee can enter or leave. So the total cash in the room is fixed, even though individual wallets fatten and thin dramatically.
The no-doors condition is the crucial one. It is exactly the requirement that no net external force acts. Open a door, and the total changes, and conservation is simply not available to you.
Now, two refinements that separate a careful student from a careless one.

First, conservation applies component-wise. If the net external force is zero only along one axis, then momentum is conserved along that axis alone. Look at the figure: a shell explodes mid-flight. Horizontally nothing external acts, so horizontal momentum is conserved. Vertically, gravity is pulling the whole time, so vertical momentum is not.

Second, the timing. During a quick collision or explosion, the internal impulsive forces are enormous compared with gravity or friction. So we treat the system as effectively isolated for that instant, and conserve momentum across it.

But stretch the window and that permission evaporates. Over a falling-and-bouncing sequence, gravity has time to change the momentum between bounces. Apply conservation only across the instant of impact, never across a long stretch of flight.

And the last habit, which is worth more than any formula here. Choosing the system correctly is everything. Pick your system so that the troublesome forces become internal, and the problem often solves itself.
<curious> इसे ऐसे सोचिए। Momentum को एक बंद कमरे में रखे पैसे की तरह देखिए, जिसमें कोई दरवाज़ा नहीं। वो कमरा आपका isolated system है।

अंदर के लोग दिन भर एक-दूसरे को cash पकड़ा सकते हैं — वही internal forces हैं — पर एक rupee भी अंदर या बाहर नहीं जा सकता। तो कमरे का total cash fixed है, भले ही individual wallets भारी और हल्के होते रहें।
'कोई दरवाज़ा नहीं' वाली शर्त ही असली शर्त है। ये ठीक वही requirement है कि net external force zero हो। एक दरवाज़ा खुला, total बदल गया, और conservation आपके हाथ से निकल गया।
अब दो बारीकियाँ जो सावधान student को लापरवाह से अलग करती हैं।

पहली, conservation component-wise लगता है। अगर net external force सिर्फ एक axis पर zero है, तो momentum सिर्फ उसी axis पर conserve होगा। Figure देखिए: एक shell उड़ते-उड़ते फटता है। Horizontally बाहर से कुछ नहीं लग रहा, तो horizontal momentum conserve है। Vertically gravity लगातार खींच रही है, तो vertical momentum नहीं।

दूसरी, timing। तेज़ collision या explosion के दौरान internal impulsive forces gravity या friction के मुक़ाबले बहुत बड़ी होती हैं। तो उस instant के लिए हम system को effectively isolated मान लेते हैं और उसके आर-पार momentum conserve कर लेते हैं।

पर window को खींचिए और ये इजाज़त उड़ जाती है। गिरने और उछलने के पूरे sequence में gravity को bounces के बीच momentum बदलने का वक़्त मिल जाता है। Conservation सिर्फ impact के instant के आर-पार लगाइए, कभी लंबी उड़ान के आर-पार नहीं।
और आखिरी आदत, जो यहाँ किसी भी formula से ज़्यादा कीमती है। System को सही चुनना ही सब कुछ है। System ऐसे चुनिए कि परेशान करने वाली forces internal बन जाएँ, और problem अक्सर खुद ही हल हो जाती है।

board_events.latex: u_1 + v_1 = v_2 + u_2 \;\Rightarrow\; u_1 - u_2 = v_2 - v_1

board_events.text: Sanity check - equal masses: the first fractions vanish and $v_1 = u_2$, $v_2 = u_1$. The bodies simply SWAP velocities.

segments.text: Our first Board derivation for this subtopic produces the elastic collision formulas - and, on the way, something more beautiful than the formulas themselves.

Two bodies of masses m one and m two move along a line with initial velocities u one and u two. After a head-on elastic collision their velocities are v one and v two. Two things are conserved: momentum, which is always conserved, and kinetic energy, because the collision is elastic.
Write momentum conservation and rearrange it to group each mass on its own side. That gives equation one: m one times the bracket u one minus v one, equals m two times the bracket v two minus u two.

Now write kinetic energy conservation, cancel the halves, group the same way, and factor each side as a difference of squares. That gives equation two, which carries the same brackets as equation one, each multiplied by a sum.
And here is the clever step, the one worth remembering long after the algebra fades. Divide equation two by equation one. The mass-and-bracket factors cancel cleanly on both sides.
What survives is startlingly simple. u one plus v one equals v two plus u two. Rearrange it, and you get: u one minus u two equals v two minus v one.

Read that in words, because it is the real prize. In an elastic collision, the relative velocity of approach equals the relative velocity of separation. The bodies separate exactly as fast as they came together. This is also why the coefficient of restitution is defined the way it is - here it equals one.
Solve that intermediate result together with the momentum equation and out come the standard pair for v one and v two. You should know these, but you should know the relative-velocity result better.

And always sanity-check. Set the masses equal. The first fractions vanish, and you get v one equals u two, v two equals u one. The bodies simply swap velocities - exactly what you see when one carrom coin strikes another head-on.
इस subtopic का पहला Board derivation elastic collision के formulas देता है — और रास्ते में, formulas से भी ख़ूबसूरत कुछ।

m one और m two mass की दो bodies एक line पर u one और u two initial velocities से चल रही हैं। Head-on elastic collision के बाद उनकी velocities v one और v two हैं। दो चीज़ें conserve हैं: momentum, जो हमेशा conserve रहता है, और kinetic energy, क्योंकि collision elastic है।
Momentum conservation लिखिए और उसे rearrange करके हर mass को अपनी side पर group कीजिए। मिलता है equation one: m one गुणा bracket u one minus v one, बराबर m two गुणा bracket v two minus u two।

अब kinetic energy conservation लिखिए, halves cancel कीजिए, उसी तरह group कीजिए, और हर side को difference of squares की तरह factor कीजिए। मिलता है equation two, जिसमें equation one वाले ही brackets हैं, हर एक के साथ एक sum गुणा।
और अब वो चालाक step, जो algebra भूल जाने के बाद भी याद रखने लायक है। Equation two को equation one से divide कीजिए। दोनों तरफ mass-and-bracket factors साफ़-साफ़ cancel हो जाते हैं।
जो बचता है वो हैरान करने वाला simple है। u one plus v one बराबर v two plus u two। Rearrange कीजिए और मिलता है: u one minus u two बराबर v two minus v one।

इसे शब्दों में पढ़िए, क्योंकि असली इनाम यही है। Elastic collision में relative velocity of approach बराबर होती है relative velocity of separation के। Bodies ठीक उतनी ही तेज़ी से अलग होती हैं जितनी तेज़ी से पास आई थीं। और इसीलिए coefficient of restitution की definition ऐसी है — यहाँ वो एक के बराबर है।
उस intermediate result को momentum equation के साथ हल कीजिए और v one और v two की standard जोड़ी निकल आती है। ये आपको आनी चाहिए, पर relative-velocity वाला result उससे बेहतर आना चाहिए।

और हमेशा sanity-check कीजिए। Masses बराबर रख दीजिए। पहले fractions गायब हो जाते हैं, और मिलता है v one बराबर u two, v two बराबर u one। Bodies बस velocities swap कर लेती हैं — ठीक वही जो carrom का एक coin दूसरे को head-on मारने पर दिखता है।

sections.title: Derivation: thrust on a rocket

board_events.text: CBSE Derivation 2: thrust on a variable-mass body
At time $t$ the rocket has mass $m$ and velocity $v$. In time $dt$ it ejects gas of mass $|dm|$ at velocity $v_{rel}$ relative to itself, and speeds up to $v + dv$.

board_events.text: Here $dm$ is NEGATIVE - the rocket loses mass. Expand, and discard the second-order term $dm\,dv$.
Thrust $= v_{rel}\,\dfrac{dm}{dt}$ - the exhaust speed times the rate of mass burn. Only two ways to raise it: eject faster, or eject quicker.
A rocket speeds up not by pushing on air, but purely by throwing mass backward. Momentum conservation in its rawest form - which is why rockets work in vacuum.

segments.text: The second derivation takes us into the variable-mass family, and it produces one of the most famous results in physics.

Set it up carefully, because the bookkeeping is where students slip. At time t the rocket has mass m and velocity v. In a short time d t it ejects gas of mass magnitude d m at velocity v relative, measured relative to the rocket, and the rocket's own speed rises to v plus d v.

Now conserve momentum for the whole system, rocket plus ejected gas, in the absence of external force. Before: m v. After: the lighter rocket carrying its new speed, plus the ejected gas carrying its own.

Two details do all the damage here. First, d m is negative, because the rocket is losing mass. Second, the ejected gas leaves at v minus v relative in the ground frame, not at v relative. Get either wrong and the sign of your thrust flips.
Expand the product, and discard the second-order term d m times d v, because it is a small number times another small number.
What remains rearranges to: m times d v by d t equals minus v relative times d m by d t. The right-hand side is the thrust - the effective forward force the engine provides.
Read what it says. Thrust equals the exhaust speed times the rate at which mass is burnt. Want more push? Throw mass faster, or throw it out quicker. Those are your only two options.
Integrate this, ignoring gravity, from initial mass m nought down to mass m, and you get the celebrated rocket equation: the speed gained equals v relative times the natural log of m nought over m.

<excited> And the physical reading is glorious. A rocket speeds up not by pushing on the air, but purely by throwing mass backward. This is momentum conservation in its rawest form - and it is exactly why rockets work in vacuum, where there is nothing at all to push against.
दूसरा derivation हमें variable-mass family में ले जाता है, और physics के सबसे मशहूर results में से एक देता है।

Setup ध्यान से कीजिए, क्योंकि students यहीं हिसाब में फिसलते हैं। Time t पर rocket का mass m है और velocity v। छोटे से time d t में वो d m magnitude की gas को v relative velocity पर बाहर फेंकता है, जो rocket के relative नापी गई है, और rocket की अपनी speed v plus d v हो जाती है।
अब पूरे system का momentum conserve कीजिए, rocket plus निकली gas, external force की गैरमौजूदगी में। पहले: m v। बाद में: हल्का rocket अपनी नई speed के साथ, plus निकली gas अपनी speed के साथ।

यहाँ दो details ही सारा नुकसान करती हैं। पहली, d m negative है, क्योंकि rocket mass खो रहा है। दूसरी, निकली gas ground frame में v minus v relative पर जाती है, v relative पर नहीं। इनमें से कोई एक गलत हुई, तो thrust का sign पलट जाएगा।
Product expand कीजिए, और second-order term d m गुणा d v छोड़ दीजिए, क्योंकि वो एक छोटी संख्या गुणा दूसरी छोटी संख्या है।
जो बचता है वो rearrange होकर बनता है: m गुणा d v by d t बराबर minus v relative गुणा d m by d t। दाईं तरफ वाला हिस्सा ही thrust है — वो effective forward force जो engine देता है।
देखिए ये क्या कह रहा है। Thrust बराबर exhaust speed गुणा mass जलने की rate। ज़्यादा धक्का चाहिए? Mass को तेज़ फेंकिए, या जल्दी-जल्दी फेंकिए। बस यही दो option हैं।
इसे integrate कीजिए, gravity छोड़कर, initial mass m nought से mass m तक, और मिलता है मशहूर rocket equation: मिली speed बराबर v relative गुणा m nought upon m का natural log।

<excited> और physical reading शानदार है। Rocket हवा को धकेलकर तेज़ नहीं होता, बल्कि सिर्फ mass को पीछे फेंककर। ये momentum conservation का सबसे कच्चा रूप है — और ठीक इसीलिए rockets vacuum में काम करते हैं, जहाँ धकेलने को कुछ है ही नहीं।

sections.title: Momentum Conservation: the formula set

board_events.text: Subtopic 2 - key formulas and definitions
SI unit of momentum: kg m s$^{-1}$. Dimensional formula: $[M^1 L^1 T^{-1}]$.

board_events.latex: v = \dfrac{m_1u_1 + m_2u_2}{m_1 + m_2} \qquad \text{(perfectly inelastic - bodies stick)}
e = \dfrac{\text{velocity of separation}}{\text{velocity of approach}} = \dfrac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2}

board_events.text: Coefficient of restitution is dimensionless, $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$. Perfectly elastic gives $e = 1$; perfectly inelastic gives $e = 0$.

segments.text: Here is the full toolkit for momentum conservation, in one place, for fast revision.
At the top sits the master statement. If the net external force is zero, the sum of m u before equals the sum of m v after. Everything below is a special case of this one line.
Momentum is measured in kilogram metres per second, with dimensional formula M to the one, L to the one, T to the minus one - identical to impulse, as we saw.
For recoil or an explosion starting from rest, the total was zero, so it stays zero. The two momenta are equal and opposite, and the lighter body always flies off faster.
For a perfectly inelastic collision, where the bodies stick together, the common velocity is the total momentum divided by the total mass. This is your Board numerical, almost every year.
For a one-dimensional elastic collision, here is the standard pair we derived. Notice the symmetry: swap the labels one and two, and one formula becomes the other.
The coefficient of restitution is the ratio of separation speed to approach speed. Note that it compares speeds - not heights, not energies. That distinction is a favourite trap.
It is dimensionless. Perfectly elastic gives e equals one, perfectly inelastic gives e equals zero, and everything real lives between them.
The velocity of the centre of mass is total momentum over total mass, and it is constant whenever the external force is zero. Remember it - it becomes your error-checker in a moment.
And finally, thrust on a variable-mass body: v relative times d m by d t. Exhaust speed times burn rate, exactly as the derivation gave us.
ये रही momentum conservation की पूरी toolkit, एक जगह, fast revision के लिए।
सबसे ऊपर master statement बैठा है। अगर net external force zero है, तो पहले m u का sum बराबर बाद में m v के sum के। नीचे जो कुछ है, वो इसी एक line का special case है।
Momentum kilogram metre per second में नापा जाता है, dimensional formula M की power one, L की power one, T की power minus one — impulse जैसा ही, जैसा हमने देखा।
Rest से शुरू होते recoil या explosion के लिए, total zero था, तो zero ही रहेगा। दोनों momenta equal और opposite हैं, और हल्की body हमेशा तेज़ उड़ती है।
Perfectly inelastic collision के लिए, जहाँ bodies चिपक जाती हैं, common velocity बराबर total momentum upon total mass। यही आपका Board numerical है, लगभग हर साल।
One-dimensional elastic collision के लिए वही standard जोड़ी है जो हमने derive की। Symmetry देखिए: labels one और two बदल दीजिए, एक formula दूसरा बन जाता है।
Coefficient of restitution separation speed upon approach speed का ratio है। ध्यान दीजिए ये speeds की तुलना करता है — heights की नहीं, energies की नहीं। यही फ़र्क़ एक favourite trap है।
ये dimensionless है। Perfectly elastic में e बराबर one, perfectly inelastic में e बराबर zero, और असली दुनिया इन दोनों के बीच रहती है।
Centre of mass की velocity बराबर total momentum upon total mass, और जब external force zero हो तब ये constant रहती है। इसे याद रखिए — थोड़ी देर में यही आपका error-checker बनेगी।
और आखिर में, variable-mass body पर thrust: v relative गुणा d m by d t। Exhaust speed गुणा burn rate, ठीक वैसा जैसा derivation ने दिया।

board_events.text: Example 1 [CBSE Board Level]

A railway wagon of mass 8000 kg moving at 2 m/s on a straight level track collides with and automatically couples to a stationary wagon of mass 12000 kg. Find their common velocity just after coupling.

board_events.text: Coupling means the wagons move TOGETHER - a perfectly inelastic collision. The track is level and the impact is brief, so external horizontal forces are negligible.
Now check whether KE is conserved: initial KE $= \frac{1}{2}(8000)(2)^2 = 16000$ J; final KE $= \frac{1}{2}(20000)(0.8)^2 = 6400$ J.
Nearly 60% of the kinetic energy was lost to the coupling - proof that this collision is inelastic.

segments.text: A Board-level classic, and the kind of question that is worth full marks if you say the right sentence before you calculate.

A railway wagon of mass eight thousand kilograms, moving at two metres per second on a straight level track, collides with and automatically couples to a stationary wagon of mass twelve thousand kilograms. Find their common velocity just after coupling.
Start with the classification, out loud, on the answer sheet. Coupling means the wagons move off together as one body. That is a perfectly inelastic collision.

Then justify the conservation. The track is level, so gravity has no horizontal component. The impact is brief, so friction has no time to matter. External horizontal forces are negligible, and momentum is conserved. Examiners give marks for that sentence.
Now the algebra, which is the easy part. Total momentum before equals total mass times the common velocity after.

Eight thousand times two, plus twelve thousand times zero, equals twenty thousand v. So sixteen thousand equals twenty thousand v, and v is zero point eight metres per second, in the original direction.

<curious> Now the part that turns a correct answer into a complete one. Check whether kinetic energy survived. Before: half times eight thousand times two squared, which is sixteen thousand joules. After: half times twenty thousand times zero point eight squared, which is six thousand four hundred joules.

Nearly sixty percent of the kinetic energy vanished into the coupling - into the clang, the heat, the deformation of the couplers. That is not a mistake in your working. That is the proof that this collision is inelastic, and momentum did not care one bit.
एक Board-level classic, और ऐसा सवाल जिसमें पूरे marks मिलते हैं अगर calculate करने से पहले आप सही वाक्य लिख दें।

आठ हज़ार kilogram का एक railway wagon, सीधे level track पर दो metre per second से चलते हुए, बारह हज़ार kilogram के खड़े wagon से टकराकर अपने आप couple हो जाता है। Coupling के ठीक बाद उनकी common velocity निकालिए।
शुरुआत classification से कीजिए, बोलकर, answer sheet पर। Coupling का मतलब है wagons एक body बनकर साथ चल पड़ते हैं। यही perfectly inelastic collision है।

फिर conservation को justify कीजिए। Track level है, तो gravity का कोई horizontal component नहीं। Impact छोटा है, तो friction को कुछ करने का वक़्त नहीं। External horizontal forces negligible हैं, और momentum conserve है। इसी वाक्य के examiners marks देते हैं।
अब algebra, जो आसान हिस्सा है। पहले का total momentum बराबर total mass गुणा बाद की common velocity।
आठ हज़ार गुणा दो, plus बारह हज़ार गुणा zero, बराबर बीस हज़ार v। तो सोलह हज़ार बराबर बीस हज़ार v, और v हुई zero point आठ metre per second, उसी original direction में।

<curious> अब वो हिस्सा जो सही answer को पूरा answer बनाता है। Check कीजिए kinetic energy बची या नहीं। पहले: half गुणा आठ हज़ार गुणा दो squared, यानी सोलह हज़ार joule। बाद में: half गुणा बीस हज़ार गुणा zero point आठ squared, यानी छह हज़ार चार सौ joule।

करीब साठ percent kinetic energy coupling में गायब हो गई — उस खनक में, heat में, couplers की deformation में। ये आपकी working की गलती नहीं है। यही सबूत है कि collision inelastic है, और momentum को इससे रत्ती भर फ़र्क़ नहीं पड़ा।

board_events.text: The shortcut: the masses are EQUAL and the collision is elastic and head-on - so the two bodies simply exchange velocities.
The three elastic special cases - instant answers

Memorize the three elastic special cases as instant answers: (1) equal masses - swap velocities. (2) heavy hits light at rest - heavy continues almost unchanged, light shoots off at about $2u$. (3) light hits heavy at rest - light bounces back at nearly $u$, heavy barely moves.
Any option claiming the striker keeps moving forward here is wrong on sight.

segments.text: Back to a N E E T speed trap, and this one punishes students who know too much rather than too little.

A carrom striker of mass fifteen grams moving at four metres per second strikes an identical stationary coin head-on. Assuming a perfectly elastic collision, what are the velocities of the striker and the coin immediately afterward?

The trap is set beautifully. Students see 'perfectly elastic' and start plugging into the full elastic-collision formulas, with those four fractions, and burn a minute on algebra under exam pressure. The mass is even given in grams, tempting you to convert.
None of it is needed. Read the setup again. The masses are equal. The collision is elastic. It is head-on. That is exactly the special case we sanity-checked in the derivation.
So the two bodies simply exchange velocities. The striker takes on the coin's velocity, which is zero. The coin takes on the striker's, which is four metres per second.
The striker stops dead, and the coin moves off at four metres per second. And notice you never used the fifteen grams at all - it was there purely as bait.
Now bank the three elastic special cases as instant answers, because one of them appears almost every year.

One: equal masses - swap velocities. Two: a heavy body hits a light one at rest - the heavy continues almost unchanged and the light shoots off at about twice the incoming speed. Three: a light body hits a heavy one at rest - the light bounces back at nearly its original speed and the heavy barely moves.

<whisper> And a free elimination for this question. Any option claiming the striker keeps moving forward is wrong on sight. If it kept moving forward while the coin also moved forward, you would need more momentum than you started with.
वापस एक N E E T speed trap पर, और ये उन students को सज़ा देता है जो कम नहीं, ज़्यादा जानते हैं।
पंद्रह gram का एक carrom striker चार metre per second से चलते हुए एक जैसे ही खड़े coin को head-on मारता है। Perfectly elastic collision मानते हुए, striker और coin की velocities तुरंत बाद क्या होंगी?

Trap बड़े सलीके से बिछा है। Students 'perfectly elastic' देखते ही पूरे elastic-collision formulas में डालने लगते हैं, उन चारों fractions के साथ, और exam pressure में एक minute algebra में जला देते हैं। Mass भी gram में दिया है, ताकि आप convert करने का मन बनाएँ।
इसमें से कुछ नहीं चाहिए। Setup दोबारा पढ़िए। Masses बराबर हैं। Collision elastic है। Head-on है। यही वो special case है जिसे हमने derivation में sanity-check किया था।
तो दोनों bodies बस velocities exchange कर लेती हैं। Striker coin की velocity ले लेता है, जो zero है। Coin striker की ले लेता है, जो चार metre per second है।
Striker वहीं रुक जाता है, और coin चार metre per second से निकल जाता है। और ध्यान दीजिए, पंद्रह gram आपने इस्तेमाल किया ही नहीं — वो सिर्फ चारे के लिए था।
अब तीनों elastic special cases instant answers की तरह याद कर लीजिए, क्योंकि इनमें से एक लगभग हर साल आता है।

एक: बराबर masses — velocities swap। दो: भारी body हल्की खड़ी को मारे — भारी लगभग बिना बदले चलती रहती है और हल्की करीब दुगनी incoming speed से निकल जाती है। तीन: हल्की body भारी खड़ी को मारे — हल्की लगभग उसी speed से वापस उछलती है और भारी मुश्किल से हिलती है।

<whisper> और इस सवाल के लिए एक मुफ़्त elimination। कोई भी option जो कहे कि striker आगे बढ़ता रहता है, वो देखते ही गलत है। अगर वो आगे बढ़ता रहे और coin भी आगे जाए, तो शुरुआत से ज़्यादा momentum चाहिए होगा।

board_events.text: This links momentum conservation (the collision) with energy conservation (the spring) - and the ORDER matters.
Step 2 - the spring. Now, and only now, use energy. The surface is frictionless, so all the kinetic energy converts to spring potential energy at maximum compression.
You CANNOT apply energy conservation through the collision - the embedding loses kinetic energy to heat. Momentum carries you through the impact; energy carries you through the spring.

segments.text: This J E E Main problem is a two-stage question, and almost everyone who fails it fails for the same reason: they use the right laws in the wrong places.

A bullet of mass ten grams travelling at two hundred metres per second embeds itself into a wooden block of mass one point nine nine kilograms resting on a frictionless horizontal surface. The block is attached to a spring of force constant eight hundred newtons per metre. Find the maximum compression of the spring.
Look at the figure and split the story in two. Stage one is the collision. Stage two is the spring. They are governed by different laws, and the order matters.
Stage one. The bullet embeds, so the bullet and block move off together - perfectly inelastic. Use momentum, and only momentum.
Zero point zero one times two hundred equals two point zero zero times v. So v is one metre per second. Notice how kindly the numbers were chosen: the total mass is exactly two kilograms.

Stage two. Now, and only now, may you use energy. The surface is frictionless, so from the moment the bullet is embedded, nothing more is lost. All the kinetic energy converts into spring potential energy at maximum compression.

Half times two times one squared, equals half times eight hundred times x squared. So one equals four hundred x squared, giving x squared as zero point zero zero two five, and x as zero point zero five metres - five centimetres.

<whisper> Now the critical insight. You cannot apply energy conservation through the collision. The embedding loses kinetic energy to heat, sound and splintered wood. If you had started with half m u squared of the bullet and set it equal to half k x squared, you would have got a badly wrong answer with beautiful handwriting.
Say it as a slogan and it will not leave you. Momentum carries you through the impact. Energy carries you through the spring. Mixing them up is the classic way this problem is failed.
ये J E E Main problem दो stage का सवाल है, और जो लोग इसमें fail होते हैं लगभग सब एक ही वजह से होते हैं: सही laws को गलत जगह लगा देते हैं।

दस gram की एक bullet दो सौ metre per second से चलते हुए एक point नौ नौ kilogram के लकड़ी के block में धँस जाती है, जो frictionless horizontal surface पर रखा है। Block आठ सौ newton per metre के spring से जुड़ा है। Spring का maximum compression निकालिए।
Figure देखिए और कहानी को दो हिस्सों में काटिए। Stage एक है collision। Stage दो है spring। इन पर अलग laws चलते हैं, और क्रम मायने रखता है।
Stage एक। Bullet धँस जाती है, तो bullet और block साथ चल पड़ते हैं — perfectly inelastic। Momentum इस्तेमाल कीजिए, और सिर्फ momentum।
Zero point zero one गुणा दो सौ बराबर दो point zero zero गुणा v। तो v हुई एक metre per second। देखिए numbers कितनी मेहरबानी से चुने गए हैं: total mass ठीक दो kilogram।

Stage दो। अब, और सिर्फ अब, आप energy इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं। Surface frictionless है, तो bullet के धँसने के बाद कुछ और नहीं खोता। पूरी kinetic energy maximum compression पर spring potential energy में बदल जाती है।

Half गुणा दो गुणा एक squared, बराबर half गुणा आठ सौ गुणा x squared। तो एक बराबर चार सौ x squared, यानी x squared हुआ zero point zero zero two five, और x हुआ zero point zero five metre — पाँच centimetre।

<whisper> अब असली insight। आप collision के आर-पार energy conservation नहीं लगा सकते। धँसने में kinetic energy heat, sound और टूटी लकड़ी में चली जाती है। अगर आपने bullet की half m u squared को half k x squared के बराबर रख दिया होता, तो सुंदर handwriting में बुरी तरह गलत answer आता।
इसे एक नारे की तरह कहिए और ये आपको छोड़ेगा नहीं। Momentum आपको impact के पार ले जाता है। Energy आपको spring के पार। इन्हें आपस में बदल देना ही इस problem को fail करने का classic तरीका है।
